channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Fine-Tuning a Small Classifier and Reporting It Honestly
item.description: A concrete walkthrough of fine-tuning a small classifier, with the splitting, baselining and reporting habits that stop good numbers from being accidental.

item.title: Why Training Data Matters More Than Parameter Count
item.description: Parameter counts sell headlines, but a model's training data quietly sets the ceiling on what it can ever learn.

item.title: Reading a Model Card Properly: What It Hides
item.description: Model cards look like accountability documents, but gaps in their reporting often matter more than what they state outright.

item.title: What Context Length Actually Buys a Model
item.description: Longer context windows promise more memory, but what you actually get is more room to search, not more skill at using what's found.

item.title: A Benchmark Is Not an Evaluation, and That Gap Matters
item.description: Topping a benchmark is not the same as being evaluated well. Confusing the two produces models that look great on paper and fail in production.

item.title: Why Two Runs of the Same Script Can Disagree
item.description: Identical scripts can still give different accuracy numbers. I unpack the hidden sources of randomness and how to control them properly.

item.title: A Worked Example of Why Models Memorise Before They Generalise
item.description: Why neural networks often nail the training set long before they learn the underlying rule, worked through with a small modular arithmetic example.

item.title: How Tokeniser Vocabulary Size Quietly Shapes Model Behaviour
item.description: One word, three tokenisations: a concrete look at how vocabulary size changes sequence length, rare word handling, and what a model actually has to learn.

item.title: Decoder-Only or Encoder-Decoder for a Small Task
item.description: A practical guide to choosing between decoder-only and encoder-decoder transformers when your dataset is small and your compute is limited.

item.title: Why 'Understanding' Is the Wrong Word for Language Models
item.description: Calling a language model's output 'understanding' hides what's actually happening and makes failures harder to diagnose. Here's a more useful way to talk about it.

item.title: Parameters vs Hyperparameters, Shown on One Small Model
item.description: Using a one-line linear regression, I show exactly which numbers are learned and which are chosen, and why mixing them up ruins your evaluation.

item.title: Why Softmax Temperature Changes Apparent Confidence
item.description: Softmax temperature reshapes probability outputs without touching predictions, which means 'confidence' is partly a calibration choice, not a pure signal.

item.title: What a Loss Function Change Really Does to Gradients
item.description: A single-point worked example showing how squared error, absolute error, and a hinge-style loss hand the optimiser completely different gradients.

item.title: Positional Encodings Versus Recurrence: Order Without Steps
item.description: Two ways to tell a model what comes before what: step-by-step recurrence, or injected positional signals. The difference shapes speed, memory, and what a model can actually learn.

item.title: How a Multi-Head Attention Block Processes One Sentence
item.description: Tracing one sentence through a multi-head attention block, step by step, with concrete numbers and no hand-waving.

item.title: Spotting a Real MLOps Certification Versus a Checklist
item.description: Most MLOps certificates test whether you can follow slides, not whether you can run a pipeline under real failure conditions. Here is how to spot the difference.

item.title: Machine Learning Salaries Versus the Actual Day Job
item.description: Job adverts sell deep learning glamour and big salaries, but most ML roles are data cleaning and stakeholder management. Learn to read the signal.

item.title: A Worked Walkthrough of Structuring and Testing a Prompt
item.description: I build a structured prompt step by step, then show how to measure whether it genuinely beat the naive version, not just felt better.

item.title: Computer Vision in Production: Why Accuracy Diverges
item.description: Demo accuracy is measured on curated frames. Shipped accuracy is measured on reality. The gap between them is predictable once you know where to look.

item.title: The Real Skill Gap After a Prompt Engineering Course
item.description: A course teaches you prompt patterns. A job teaches you that prompts fail silently, unevenly, and expensively in production.
